events.title: Afonso I of Portugal takes Lisbon after a four-month siege
events.description: With crusader help, Afonso I, the first king of Portugal, ended a siege begun on 1 July and took Lisbon from the Moors. The siege, seen as pivotal in the Reconquista, was one of the few Christian victories of the Second Crusade.

events.title: Geoffrey Chaucer dies in London
events.description: Geoffrey Chaucer died, according to the date on his tomb in Westminster Abbey. His Canterbury Tales, written in English rather than French or Latin, helped establish English as a literary language.
events.html: Geoffrey Chaucer died, according to the date on his tomb in Westminster Abbey. His Canterbury Tales, written in English rather than French or Latin, helped establish English as a literary language.

events.title: Henry V defeats a larger French army at Agincourt
events.description: Henry V's outnumbered and exhausted army, largely archers, defeated the French at Agincourt as heavily armoured knights struggled across muddy ground. Many French nobles were killed or captured.
events.html: Henry V's outnumbered and exhausted army, largely archers, defeated the French at Agincourt as heavily armoured knights struggled across muddy ground. Many French nobles were killed or captured.

events.title: George III becomes king of Great Britain
events.description: George II died suddenly at Kensington Palace, and his 22-year-old grandson succeeded as George III. His 60-year reign saw the loss of the American colonies and victory over Napoleonic France.
events.html: George II died suddenly at Kensington Palace, and his 22-year-old grandson succeeded as George III. His 60-year reign saw the loss of the American colonies and victory over Napoleonic France.

events.title: The Light Brigade charges at Balaclava
events.description: A misunderstood order sent British light cavalry charging down a valley ringed by Russian guns. About 270 of some 670 riders were killed or wounded, and Tennyson's poem made the charge a byword for courage and blunder.

events.title: Zagonyi's Union cavalry wins the First Battle of Springfield
events.description: Near Springfield, Missouri, Major Charles Zagonyi, commander of the bodyguard of General Frémont, won a minor Union victory over Missouri State Guard recruits through a charge widely covered by the media. Federal troops occupied the city two days later.

events.title: Union troops defeat Sterling Price's Confederates at Marais des Cygnes
events.description: After their defeat at Westport on 23 October, Sterling Price's Confederate raiders withdrew into Kansas; Union troops then defeated them at Marais des Cygnes in Linn County, at Mine Creek and at the Marmiton River.

events.title: Japan launches its first organised kamikaze attacks
events.description: During the Battle of Leyte Gulf, Japanese pilots deliberately crashed their aircraft into American ships, sinking the escort carrier St. Lo. Suicide attacks became a central Japanese tactic for the rest of the war.
